topics.definition: A graph is a non-linear data structure consisting of vertices connected by edges.
Vertices (nodes) are points and edges are connections between them.
tips: Edges may be directed or undirected.

topics.definition: A directed graph has edges with a specific direction.
An undirected graph has edges without direction.
Weighted graphs assign values to edges, while unweighted graphs do not.
tips: Weights often represent cost or distance.

topics.definition: Graphs can be represented using an adjacency matrix or adjacency list.
tips: Adjacency lists save memory for sparse graphs.

topics.definition: BFS visits nodes level by level using a queue.
tips: Finds shortest path in unweighted graphs.

topics.definition: DFS explores as deep as possible before backtracking.
Graphs are used in navigation, social networks, computer networks and scheduling.
tips: Graphs are widely used in AI and networking.

topics.definition: Common programs include BFS, DFS, shortest path and minimum spanning tree.
